findings.title: Preserve wall request semantics through the candidate bridge
findings.why_it_matters: Forwarder silently removes all request headers except Authorization and Content-Type; it also handles only GET/POST. A negative test for an invalid X-Api-Key can pass because the bridge turns that request into a missing-key request, even if the application wrongly accepts the invalid supplied key. PUT returns bridge-generated501 without exercising candidate. The wall verdict therefore can describe a different request than the signed scenario.
findings.evidence: Executed AST-extracted exact Forwarder from PR1 c97b52ef; X-Api-Key was absent from captured candidate request, Authorization retained; PUT produced501 and no candidate transport call.
findings.suggested_fix: Forward end-to-end headers while replacing/filtering Host, Connection and framing headers; forward supported request methods or reject unsupported scenario methods explicitly before wall evaluation. Add a negative control distinguishing invalid versus absent custom auth header and method forwarding.
